messages:
sophia: Quick heads-up — ran the fused-attn + QKV-pack run on A100 (driver 525) with the new kernel-selector; noticing a small regression for seq<=64 workloads. runcmd / perf snippets below.

sophia: baseline (old selector / epilogue-merge disabled): p50=12.3ms p95=18.9ms tokens/sec=2.1k
new selector (prefer fused qkvpack w/ epilogue fusion): p50=13.9ms p95=22.8ms tokens/sec=1.9k

raj: ugh. is the regression uniform across batch sizes/seq? or is it short-seq only? :thinking:

sophia: mostly short-seq (8/16/32). longer seq (>=128) is fine, sometimes slightly better. Hypothesis: extra branch in epilogue+pack path increases warp divergence on tiny microbatches and thrashes L1 / store coalescing.

mike: interesting. did you capture perf counters? warp occupancy / l1_miss? also which cu sched config?

sophia: yep pasted a small perflog: 
```
L1_TEX_CACHE_MISS: 18.2% (old) -> 27.9% (new)
Shared_Load_Stall: +13%
SM_Occupancy: 61% (old) -> 58% (new)
Branch_Mispredicts: +33%
```

sophia: also saw more 64B store partials when KV-cache prefetching kicks in — looks like prefetch addresses sometimes cross warp-aligned stores, causing split writes.

lisa: could be the prefetch heuristic interacting with packed QKV layout. If we prefetch per-head vs per-token ordering changes address stride. We should try prefetch stride = head_size * sizeof(float16) vs current contiguous token-major prefetch.

raj: +1 to trying alternate prefetch strides. we should also test disabling epilogue branch merge for seq<=32 in selector (cheap rule) while we fix the micro-ops. quick AB test config idea: 
```
kernel_selector:
  rules:
    - when: seq_len <= 32 and batch_tokens <= 2048
      prefer: epilogue_separate_qkvpack
    - else: prefer: fused_qkv_epilogue
```

mike: sounds good. I'll spin a bench with stride swapped and the selector rule. can we add a microtrace around the write path? something like: 
```
TRACE: prefetch_addr, store_size, warp_id, head_idx
```
so we can see misaligned store patterns.

sophia: added the trace hook locally and repro'd split stores — confirming misaligned stores correlate with head-major prefetch. when we switch to head-contiguous prefetch addresses, partial store count drops ~60% and p50 goes to 12.6ms. p95 still a bit high (20.1ms) — looks like branch mispredictions remain.

lisa: for branch side, can we try a small epilogue fast-path: single-instruction sigmoid/scale fused path for common case (no rope, no bias) and fallback to general fused path. that would avoid the branch in hot path.

raj: +1. also worth checking if ROTARY precompute (apply earlier in the pipeline) lets us remove rope branch entirely in epilogue. precompute cost tradeoff probably small for short seq.

infra-bot: CI: perf-bench/eng-runtime/2105014321-1 FAILED — regression detected p95 +12% on short-seq tests. See: https://ci.redwood.company/builds/2105014321/perf-bench/details

mike: I'll post results back in ~30m. if the selector rule + stride fix removes regression we can land a conservative selector change to avoid user impact.

sophia: thanks — if anything else reproduces locally ping me and I'll share the trace output (tiny csv). planning to try lisa's fast-path patch next. :sparkles:
